hints: Notice the prefix G in 128 GB and recall what power of 10 the SI prefix giga represents.
Write $1 \text{ GB} = 10^9 \text{ B}$, so multiply 128 by $10^9$ to get the capacity in bytes.
Rewrite 128 as $1.28 \times 10^2$ and then combine the powers of 10 to match the $1.28 \times 10^n \text{ B}$ form in the options.
walkthrough: Identify the given value: $128 \text{ GB}$, where B is the unit byte and G is the SI prefix giga.
State the prefix rule: giga means $10^9$, so $1 \text{ GB} = 1 \times 10^9 \text{ B}$.
Set up the conversion: capacity $= 128 \times 10^9 \text{ B}$.
Rewrite 128 in standard form: $128 = 1.28 \times 10^2$, so capacity $= 1.28 \times 10^2 \times 10^9 \text{ B} = 1.28 \times 10^{11} \text{ B}$.
Check units and size: the unit is now B and $10^{11}$ is correct for about a hundred billion bytes. This is option B.
